Only the two weak concepts are retaught. Do not ask about the other first-round concepts or detailed chemical mechanisms.

payload.explanation_text: Compare straight and bent tails. Saturated fatty acid tails fit closely together. Double bonds bend unsaturated tails, leaving more room for movement and increasing fluidity. Cholesterol helps balance that movement. When the membrane is very fluid, cholesterol restrains movement; in the cold, it prevents excessive stiffening. It buffers fluidity rather than always increasing it.

concepts.name: Saturated vs. unsaturated fatty acids
concepts.taught_summary: Saturated tails pack closely; double bonds kink unsaturated tails, hindering close packing and increasing fluidity.

concepts.name: Cholesterol as a fluidity buffer
concepts.taught_summary: Cholesterol restrains movement in a very fluid membrane and prevents excessive stiffening in the cold.
